concrete_work.unit_description: per square foot for slabs, per linear foot for footings, per cubic yard for pours

large_driveway.description: 1,000 sq ft - extended driveway with parking area

sidewalk_100ft.description: 400 sq ft - 4ft wide x 100ft long sidewalk

concrete_3000psi.notes: Standard 3000 PSI concrete mix, suitable for most residential slabs

concrete_4000psi.notes: 4000 PSI concrete, more durable for driveways and high-traffic

concrete_5000psi.notes: High-strength 5000 PSI, for heavy loads or freeze-thaw climates

fiber_reinforced_concrete.notes: Concrete with synthetic fibers, reduces cracking
fiber_reinforced_concrete.typical_use: driveways, patios where cracking is concern

rebar_reinforcement.notes: Steel rebar grid, typically #4 bar @ 18 inch centers

wire_mesh_reinforcement.notes: 6x6 10/10 welded wire mesh, lighter than rebar

vapor_barrier.notes: 6mil plastic sheeting under slab to prevent moisture

gravel_base_4_inch.notes: 4 inch compacted gravel base, crushed stone

gravel_base_6_inch.notes: 6 inch compacted gravel base for driveways

concrete_finisher_rate.notes: BLS 2024 data, skilled trade with overhead

basic_slab_pour_finish.notes: Includes forming, pouring, screeding, floating, troweling, basic broom finish

driveway_pour_finish.notes: Driveway-specific: thicker slab (6in), control joints, proper slope for drainage

stamped_concrete.notes: Decorative stamped pattern (stone, brick, slate patterns), requires special skills and timing

stained_concrete.notes: Acid stain or water-based stain after curing, includes sealer

polished_concrete.notes: Grinding and polishing existing slab, multiple passes with progressively finer grits

exposed_aggregate.notes: Surface retarder and washing to expose aggregate, decorative finish

epoxy_coating.notes: Garage floor epoxy coating, includes surface prep, primer, epoxy, and flake broadcast

concrete_sealing.notes: Penetrating sealer or acrylic sealer application

excavation_and_grading.notes: Excavate to proper depth, grade for drainage, compact subgrade

formwork_setup.notes: Build and stake forms, includes materials (2x4 or 2x6 lumber, stakes)

demolition_existing_concrete.notes: Break up existing concrete, includes labor only (disposal separate)

concrete_disposal.notes: Haul away and dump fee for broken concrete

hand_finishing_edges.notes: Edging tool for clean borders, hand troweling

basic_patio_12x16.notes: 192 sq ft patio, 4 inch thick, broom finish, includes 4in gravel base

stamped_patio_12x16.notes: 192 sq ft stamped concrete patio with color, decorative pattern

single_car_driveway_12x30.notes: 360 sq ft driveway, 6in thick with rebar, control joints, proper slope

two_car_driveway_20x30.notes: 600 sq ft two-car driveway, 6in thick, rebar, broom finish

sidewalk_4ft_x_50ft.notes: 200 sq ft sidewalk, 4in thick, broom finish

garage_floor_20x20.notes: 400 sq ft garage floor, 4in thick, vapor barrier, smooth steel trowel finish

garage_floor_epoxy_coating.notes: 400 sq ft garage floor epoxy coating (existing slab), includes surface prep and two-part epoxy

red_flags: Charging >$8/sq ft for basic broom-finish slab labor (should be $3-6/sq ft)
Claiming you need 8+ inches thick for residential driveway (6 inches is standard, 4 inches for light use)
Requiring 5000 PSI concrete for basic patio (3000 PSI is fine for most residential)
Pushing stamped concrete when you asked for basic finish (huge markup)
Charging separately for control joints (should be included in labor)
Adding 20%+ waste factor (concrete is ordered to exact amount, 5-10% waste typical)
Claiming rebar required for patio (wire mesh usually sufficient)
Requiring 8+ inch gravel base (4-6 inches standard for most applications)
Charging >$150/CY for standard concrete delivered (should be $110-145/CY)
Insisting on fiber-reinforced concrete for everything (standard concrete fine for most jobs)
Claiming soil conditions require special foundation work without testing
Charging >$5/sq ft for concrete demolition (should be $2-5/sq ft)
Adding 'mobilization fee' >$300 for standard residential job
Bundling unnecessary drainage systems into quote
Charging per hour instead of per square foot (allows padding)

common_upsells.rebar_everywhere: Rebar when wire mesh would work
common_upsells.fiber_reinforcement: Fiber concrete when standard is fine
common_upsells.excessive_base: 8+ inch gravel base when 4-6 inches works
common_upsells.vapor_barrier_always: Vapor barrier when not needed (not under outdoor slabs)
common_upsells.sealer_immediately: Sealer before concrete fully cured (wait 28+ days)
common_upsells.unnecessary_saw_cuts: Excessive control joints beyond what's needed

cost_factors.access: Poor access requiring wheelbarrow transport adds 30-50% labor
cost_factors.sloped_site: Significant slope requires more excavation/forming, adds 20-40%
cost_factors.soil_conditions: Poor soil may require deeper base or soil stabilization
cost_factors.weather: Cold weather pours require blankets and heaters, adds 15-25%
cost_factors.hot_weather: Hot weather requires accelerators and extra care, adds 10-15%
cost_factors.pump_truck: If concrete truck can't reach, pump truck adds $400-800
cost_factors.thickness: Each additional inch adds ~25% to concrete cost
cost_factors.finishing: Decorative finishes (stamped, stained, exposed) add 50-150% to labor

technical_specs.control_joints: Should be spaced at 2x thickness in feet (4 inch slab = 8ft spacing)
technical_specs.curing_time: Allow 7 days before light use, 28 days for full cure
technical_specs.slope_for_drainage: Minimum 1/4 inch per foot for proper water runoff

regional_notes.cold_climates: Requires 4000+ PSI concrete, air entrainment for freeze-thaw resistance
regional_notes.hot_climates: May need retarders in summer to slow curing, shade during finishing
regional_notes.high_water_table: May require drainage system or elevated base
regional_notes.expansive_soils: Some soils expand/contract, may need engineered base or post-tension
regional_notes.seismic_zones: May require additional reinforcement per local codes
